items.topic: How should the CLI signal human vs agent caller for decision-accept?
items.context: The PATCH handler treats X-Caller-ID empty/'ui-user' as a human (handlers.go:2226-2227); approval-mode teams block agents from setting accepted/rejected. The CLI must let a human walker accept a decision while still being usable by automated agents in yolo mode.

options.label: Default human; opt-in agent via --as-agent <id>
options.rationale: Matches the morning-vision-walk use case (human at terminal). Sending no X-Caller-ID makes the API treat the caller as human. Explicit --as-agent for automation.

options.label: Default to env var PROMPT_MANAGER_CALLER_ID; --human flag forces human
options.rationale: Auto-detect when running inside an agent shell. Slightly magical and easy to misconfigure.

options.label: Always require explicit --caller human|<agent-id>
options.rationale: Most explicit, no surprises. Costs an extra flag on every invocation, including the common human path.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.freeform: Can assume agents are spawned through agent-manager, which I believe has an identity system via env vars. This can be used to detect agents and get their specific info if needed, and if set up is likely used by a few scenarios already if you want to see some implementation examples

items.context: PATCH payload (heartbeat/models.go:207-220) accepts: decision, rationale, context, status, supersedes, topic, description, options, selected, freeform, notes. The morning-vision-walk skill needs at least selected + notes. Broader exposure costs surface area but matches 'thin wrapper' principle.

options.label: Minimal: --selected, --notes
options.rationale: Smallest surface that unblocks the skill. Add more later if needed.

options.label: Decision-acceptance fields: --selected, --notes, --freeform, --status (default 'accepted')
options.rationale: Covers the realistic acceptance flow (including 'Other' freeform answers from workshop rounds) without exposing fields that belong to decision-add (rationale, context, options).

options.label: Full PATCH surface: every field in the model
options.rationale: Strict thin-wrapper purism. Risks letting decision-accept overwrite topic/options, which is really decision-update territory.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.topic: What 'CLI parity' means for the audit and the test
items.context: 166 v1 endpoints exist. Some are health/auth/internal and don't make sense as CLI commands. Others (e.g., GET /teams/{id} vs GET /teams/{id}/members) overlap conceptually with one CLI command (`team show`).

options.label: Strict 1:1 — every (method,path) needs its own subcommand
options.rationale: Maximally explicit. Forces a lot of low-value subcommands (health checks, internal probes).

options.label: Coverage — every endpoint must be reachable via at least one CLI subcommand; explicit allowlist for endpoints intentionally without CLI parity
options.rationale: Matches the actual goal: a skill author can do anything from the CLI. Allowlist documents intentional gaps with rationale.

options.label: Domain-only — every domain must have a CLI; individual endpoint coverage not enforced
options.rationale: Lowest friction, but reproduces today's bug: decision-accept missing inside an existing 'team' domain would still slip through.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.topic: How should the parity check be implemented?
items.context: Routes are registered as plain `v1.HandleFunc(...)` in api/main.go (no central registry). CLI subcommands are `case "name":` lines in per-domain route() switches. We need a check that runs in CI without standing up the full API server.

options.label: Go test that AST-parses api/main.go for HandleFunc calls and AST-parses each cli/<domain>/*.go for route() cases, then diffs against an allowlist
options.rationale: No production code change, runs as `go test`, deterministic. Most aligned with existing patterns.

options.label: Refactor main.go to register routes via a central RouteRegistry slice; test reads the slice
options.rationale: Cleaner long-term, but expands scope into an API-side refactor that touches every handler package.

options.label: Shell script + grep, invoked from CI separately
options.rationale: Cheap to write, but lives outside `go test` and adds a CI-only failure mode.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.topic: How to handle CLI gaps discovered by the audit (beyond decision-accept)
items.context: The audit will likely find more missing subcommands. They could all land in this PR, or be split into follow-up items. The P1 blocker is specifically decision-accept; the audit + CI guard are the systemic fix.

options.label: Land everything in this item: decision-accept + all newly-discovered missing subcommands + CI guard
options.rationale: One shot, lowest coordination cost, ensures CI guard turns green immediately.

options.label: Land decision-accept + CI guard with allowlist seeded from current gaps; file follow-up backlog items per missing subcommand
options.rationale: Unblocks morning-vision-walk fastest; allowlist makes the gap list explicit and trackable; avoids a giant PR.

options.label: Land decision-accept now; defer audit + CI guard to a separate item
options.rationale: Smallest patch, but leaves the systemic root cause unfixed and contradicts the original P1 framing.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach

items.text: The team domain CLI lives in a single file (cli/teams/teams.go, ~2600 lines) with a central route() switch at line 539. Sibling commands decision-add (618) and decision-list (620) already exist; decision-accept slots in between them with no structural changes. The PATCH handler is at api/heartbeat/handlers.go:2115 and accepts selected/notes/freeform/status — no schema change needed.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md scaffold with all mandatory sections populated from existing code. Set acceptance_allow to scenarios/prompt-manager/{cli,api,docs/reference}/** and acceptance_deny to secrets/**. Strategy phased into: (1) decision-accept subcommand, (2) audit + missing subcommands, (3) CI parity test, (4) docs. Five decisions surfaced in this round to converge on caller-identity model, flag surface, parity definition, check implementation, and PR-scope strategy.
